entries.note: DOI resolves to Lin 2009 AAC (PMID 19171797, epub 2009-01). Quote verbatim in abstract. Untested opener fine; model_first_use_year 2009 is a late proxy (replicon used for the class well before simeprevir).

Reesink 2010 Gastroenterology (PMID 19852962, epub 2009-10). Quote verbatim. Viral RNA proximal tier correct. Minor: note says 'within 5 days'; abstract gives median 6 days to maximal reduction (5 days dosing). n=6 patients.
Quote verbatim in Lin 2009 abstract; rat plasma/liver above replicon EC99 is the stated exposure target.

entries.rule: dose table row 'reached, drug worked'; evidence rule 7
entries.note: Quote verbatim, but abstract shows no exposure vs EC99, and 'drug worked' was only a 5-day viral decline in 2009; efficacy known from Olysio label 2013. Alternative: glecaprevir 70x NOAEL (209394 PharmR, verbatim) as margin_stated same, 2017.
entries.adjudication_note: Dose table row 'target reached' and rule 6: dose scores whether the stated once-daily/EC99 regimen was reached, not whether the drug worked (efficacy). Reesink 2009: 'pharmacokinetics supported a once daily dosing regimen'. Same, dated 2009, not 2013.

entries.note: Quote verbatim in Lin 2009 abstract; replicon combination prediction, untested opener.

Bundle label: QUEST pooled SVR12 80% (419/521) vs 50% (132/264); Q80K 58% vs 84%; replicon Q80K FC 11 in 12.4; 5.1 cross-refs 12.4. NCT01289782 results posted 2014-06-04 confirmed. An earlier member 'same' exists (see missing).
Label 13.2 quote verbatim; 28x dog and 0.2x rat testes figures verified in 13.1/13.2.

208261 PharmR quote verbatim; FDA states the match (comparison_stated true). No hepatobiliary effect at >=3x clinical exposure verified; label 5.1: ALT elevation in 1% of subjects. Paritaprevir review (biliary target organ) does not contradict.

Quote verbatim (PMC3028818 full text): chimps fell >5 log10 at 5 mg/kg bid x7d. But vaniprevir patient monotherapy (4.6 log10 day 8, 700 mg bid) was public at AASLD Oct 2008 (natap.org/2008/AASLD/AASLD_09.htm); 'no patient comparison yet' is false in 2010.
entries.adjudication_note: RULE QUESTION: decision 10 requires a model result that post-dates AND is motivated by the patient result. Olsen 2010 chimp work post-dates vaniprevir patient data (AASLD 2008) but targets combination cure; does post-dating alone make it retro?

entries.note: Lawitz 2013 quote verbatim in abstract; direction matches (chimp >5 vs patient 1.8-4.6 log10, full text quantifies chimp side). Patient result public 2008, chimp record first 2010 (Liverton 2010 has only uninfected-chimp PK), so no prospective prediction is on record: retro.

entries.note: Kan 2015 (PMID 26562322, epub 2015-11-12) quote verbatim in abstract; untested correct. Europe PMC search found no patient report of DCV+ASV response after simeprevir failure before Nov 2015 (first: Kan 2016; Hepatol Res Mar 2016, n=5).

Kan 2016 (PMID 27651415) quote verbatim in abstract; post-dates the 2015 mouse prediction, so same, not retro. The 2016 mouse arm is post hoc and correctly unscored. Caveat: retrospective single-centre cohort, not a trial primary endpoint.
Reddy 2012 AAC (PMID 22470110, PMC3370793, epub 2012-04-02) resolves; quote verbatim in abstract. Untested opener at first use is fine; in-silico VK model distinct from replicon and rat-PK tracks.

entries.rule: retrodiction that failed to reproduce human data is contra; one drug's contra beats another's same
entries.note: Full text read. Table 2 footnote d confirms predictions use the LPR model; ABT-450/r 50 mg -4.07 vs -1.9 verbatim. retro=true correct (all PI monotherapy data predated). 'perform significantly better' phrase not found; danoprevir misses are 1.7 log10 (day-2 data), not >2.

missing: Efficacy: vaniprevir phase II (Manns 2012 Hepatology, doi:10.1002/hep.25743, epub 2012-07-17): primary endpoint RVR 68.8-83.3% vs 5.6% placebo (P<0.001). An earlier member 'same' (paired with vaniprevir replicon data), so the efficacy cell turns 'same' in 2012, not 2013.

Dose: glecaprevir 6-month rat NOAEL gives a 70x exposure margin at 300 mg (209394 PharmR: 'This provides an exposure margin of 70X'), which held in patients. This is a margin_stated 'same' (2017) and could carry the dose cell if dose entry 2 is not accepted.

Safety (no status change expected): FDA clinical hold on sovaprevir, June 2013, for grade 3-4 ALT elevations in a healthy-volunteer DDI study with atazanavir/ritonavir (Achillion 10-K, https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1070336/000119312514089075/d645073d10k.htm; https://www.fiercepharma.com/regulatory/fda-slaps-a-clinical-hold-on-achillion-hep-c-drug). The harm came from conditions the model never tested, so 'untested'; the draft's judgement should mention it.
rule_questions: Dose table 'reached, drug worked': does a phase 1 viral-load response count as 'worked', so the entry is dated at phase 1, or must the efficacy primary endpoint have read out first? Also, can a dose entry be 'same' when the source never reports exposure against the model's numeric target (EC99)?
Q80K: the replicon fold change was measured on baseline clinical isolates at the same time as the phase 3 trials. Is this a prospective model prediction or a retrodiction (retro)?

Hepatotoxicity seen only under a drug interaction (sovaprevir with atazanavir/r in healthy volunteers; paritaprevir with ethinyl estradiol): no rule says whether a DDI-driven harm the animals were never dosed under counts as the model's silence being contradicted or as untested.

Models check: a routine preclinical model (HCV chimpanzee monotherapy) whose run date is unstated and whose first record (2010) post-dates a public patient result (AASLD 2008), but which was not motivated by it. Rule 10 requires both 'post-dates' and 'motivated by'; scored retro here on the record date.
